newsitem.title: INDIA: India 95/96 real GDP rose 7.1 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: India 95/96 real GDP rose 7.1 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Indian gross domestic product (GDP), adjusted for inflation, increased 7.1 percent in 1995/96 (April-March) over the previous fiscal year, a Planning Ministry official said on Thursday.
The official, who asked not to be named, said the ministry would release official estimates of national income, consumption, expenditure, savings and capital formation for 1995/96 later on Thursday.
GDP at factor cost and at constant prices was estimated in 1995/96 at 2,742 billion rupees, up from 2,561 billion in 1994/95, the official said.
GDP increased by 7.2 percent in 1994/95 over the previous fiscal year, he said.
At current prices unadjusted for inflation, GDP grew by 14.8 percent in 1995/96, he said.

At constant prices, national income for 1995/96 was estimated at 2,367 billion rupees, up 6.9 percent from 2,214 billion in 1994/95, the official said. At current prices, the increase in national income was 14.5 percent, he said.

The official said the 1995/96 real GDP growth rate of 7.1 percent was mainly due to high growth in manufacturing, electricity, trade, hotels, restaurants, communication, railways and transport other than railways.
He said there was higher growth in public administration, defence and other personal service sectors.

There was a decline of 0.4 percent in agricultural production in 1995/96, mainly attributable to a fall in production of rice (-2.6 percent), wheat (-4.8 percent), coarse cereal (-1.0 percent) and pulses (- 5.5 percent), the official said.
There was an increase in production of oilseeds (+4.5 percent), cotton (+10.1 percent) and sugarcane (+2.7 percent).
